purpose: "copied by/for a mumukṣu (seeker of liberation); no explicit svārtha/parārtha"
notes:
I have recorded the era as VS, not NS. The "miti … roja" formula and the copy being made at Galkoṭ in western Nepal point to Vikrama Saṃvat, which makes VS 1887 = c. 1830 CE. As NS, 1887 would be impossible.

The scribe's name and titles: "vīrabhadrasādhaka" is read as the name Vīrabhadra plus the title sādhaka. The catalogue gives the whole compound, Vīrabhadrasādhaka, as the scribe's name. "mumukṣuṇe(!)" is a garbled form, probably meant as an instrumental (mumukṣuṇā), so it describes the scribe. It could also be read as a dative ("for a mumukṣu"), which would make it the copy's intended recipient, but the scribe reading seems more likely. "litaṃ(!)" stands for likhitaṃ.

The place name is unclear. The colophon reads "rāmadilamuṇyāśrame"; the catalogue gives "Rāmadilapuṇyāśrama", so "muṇya" is probably a mistake for "puṇya". "daśruśaile" is unclear; it may be a corruption of a word for a hill or mountain near Galkoṭ.

Aṣṭāvakra is named as the author of the text ("aṣṭāvakramuniviracite"). I left him out because he is a mythical sage, not a historical person.
